topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
consensus_response: V-band offers superior performance in inter-satellite communication due to its lower atmospheric attenuation and higher data rates. Its continuous frequency range maximizes bandwidth and minimizes interference, enabling longer line-of-sight paths and improved signal strength. While optical systems excel in specific scenarios like deep space applications, V-band's advantages make it the dominant choice for most mission-critical inter-satellite communication needs.
reference_context: V-band (57-66 GHz) offers a clear advantage over optical systems for inter-satellite communication due to its ability to penetrate Earth's atmosphere with minimal signal degradation.  This translates to longer range, increased data rates, and reduced latency. V-band's continuous frequency range also minimizes interference from other satellites and ground stations, making it ideal for mission-critical applications where reliability and performance are paramount.
